findings.reason: The protected source is a robust expert parser: one monotonic cursor reads complete signed integers, mutable stack frames expose the next child slot, and explicit empty parentheses advance that slot without allocating a node. The iterative structure avoids recursion limits while staying direct, so no inert candidate is materially justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 536 and its Python string-to-optional-TreeNode contract. The app source defines the required local equivalent of LeetCode's injected model, handles empty input, negative and multi-digit values, left-before-right attachment, explicit missing children, and the complete nested encoding.

The immutable native source is bound to verified submission 2065290713. It and the protected app source have identical empty-input return, stack/root/cursor state, parenthesis branches, empty-child slot increment, closing-pop rule, signed digit scan, parent attachment, mutable slot advancement, frame push, and final root return; only the model and native wrapper differ.

The left-chain encodings contain 116, 372, and 1168 characters, span more than 10x, and force a matching-parenthesis parser to rescan nested suffixes. The protected source passed all 10 correctness cases and all three performance tiers, including the legal 30,000-character boundary. A correct recursive rescan-and-slice control passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict with relative growth exponent +0.99 and a 61.94x largest runtime ratio.

The current-targeted Approach exactly explains signed integer tokenization, frame contents, child-slot mutation, empty-child handling, closing-parenthesis context restoration, and preorder correctness. It defines string length and tree height and accounts for disjoint numeric slices in the O(n) time and O(h) auxiliary-space bounds.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the authenticated Premium statement. It preserves the integer-plus-zero/one/two-child grammar, left-child-first rule, empty input allowance, all three source examples, all three displayed constraints, negative-root example, and source order. The source tree image was independently recreated as an accessible Mermaid diagram with identical node and child relationships.

coverage: All three authenticated Premium source examples now appear first and in source order with their exact encodings and level-order trees. The two missing full-tree examples, including the negative-root form, were restored.
The invented right-only sample was relabelled as a trial, the simplified negative sample was replaced by the exact source example, and both formerly hidden correctness cases are now visible trials.
Boundaries cover empty and 30,000-character encodings, one and 10,000 nodes, signed values -1073741824 and 1073741824, leaves, balanced trees, skewed trees, and multi-digit tokens.

Material grammar semantics cover left-before-right attachment, two children, a missing right child, an explicit empty left child before a right child, nested subtrees, mixed signs, and returning None for the empty encoding.

An independent recursive grammar parser and level-order serializer verified all ten correctness cases and all three benchmark outputs. The protected implementation also agreed on 1,291 exhaustive small signed trees and 1,000 randomized trees.
All ten correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 116-, 372-, and 1,168-character left-chain workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
